content:
Maya: heads-up — after flipping on continuous-batching v2 for a week, we see small regressions on streamed short responses (<=16 tokens). latency tail up ~12-15ms on p95 for interactive flows.
Jian: hmm, do you have a repro workload or a timeline?
Maya: yes — internal slackbot + chat widget. spikes align with high-admit small bursts. I pushed a short profiler trace to the perf bucket.
Eli: can you paste the hot-path flame? quick glance suggested kernel switch overhead on very short decodes (small-kernel fallback).
Maya: pasted snippet below — notice the kernel handshake + partial-decode scheduling cost:
```
0.000s dispatch -> select_kernel(small, prefer_fast)
0.006s kernel_init + copy
0.010s partial_decode_schedule(wait_for_batch)
0.028s send_stream_chunk
```
Maya: that 10–18ms window seems to dominate for 1-3 token streams.
Sofia: interesting — KV cache warmup looks fine in headroom graphs, but queues show a lot of tiny batches getting admitted and then flushed early. could be our flush cadence + token budget heuristic.
Jian: theory: continuous-batching opts to wait to aggregate a tiny batch to improve throughput, but streaming flush logic preempts once any token ready -> forces kernel init overhead for small kernel repeatedly. kernel selection toggles between small and standard which adds cost.
perf-bot: profile summary (avg over 5000 short streams):
- kernel_select: 5.8ms
- kernel_init + memcpy: 6.2ms
- scheduling wait: 3.4ms
- send/serialize: 2.1ms
- total p95 extra: ~17.5ms
ops-bot: deploy note: rollout on canary 3 clusters, no regressions flagged by infra SLO alerts besides perf.
Eli: could we reduce kernel-select churn by caching selection per-admission-window? i.e., if batches in the same 50ms slice have similar seq-len distribution, reuse kernel handle instead of re-init.
Jian: yes — small optimization: sticky-kernel per-device for N ms. fallback: clear when sequence distribution changes >20%. cheap to implement in runtime.
Maya: another angle: increase stream prefetch threshold so that flush cadence prefers coalescing tiny writes for 8–16 tokens up to a 12ms micro-window. prevents immediate flush after first token.
Sofia: tradeoff: adds jitter to earliest tokens. but for chat widget the 1st token latency matters. maybe a hybrid: soft-drip for token 1 with micro-send if no other tokens arrive in 6ms, otherwise wait.
Eli: also look at KV cache partial-decode: when KV miss we do sync prefetch that blocks kernel_init. If we shadow-fetch KV in admission phase, we can avoid blocking during partial-decode.
Maya: experimented locally with two knobs: sticky-kernel-ms=40 and stream-first-token-drip=6ms. Results on canary: p95 down by 9ms, avg unaffected. tail improved for <=16 tokens.
perf-bot: experiment run id: run-2026-03-15-09: metrics: p50: +0.5ms, p95: -9.2ms, p99: -6.1ms.
Jian: sounds promising. let's not forget fairness: when sticky-kernel holds handles, ensure we don't starve different model variants on same device. set capacity limit N handles per-device.
Sofia: logging request: add metric for kernel-switches/sec and sticky-hits to console dashboards. helps correlating with SLO blips.
Maya: PR drafted: runtime: add sticky-kernel window + stream drip config + KV shadow prefetch flag. code in branch runtime/drip-sticky-kernel.
Eli: can you add microbench harness: 1k small streams in parallel with varying inter-token gaps (2ms..20ms). want to validate across quantized kernels too.
Maya: yup — adding harness and small test clusters. planning canary tomorrow.
Jian: action items: (1) merge metric + logging (Sofia), (2) finish harness + run (Eli), (3) review PR and safety limits (Jian + Maya).
Sofia: ack. will add dashboard panels and alert if kernel_switches/sec > baseline * 3.
Maya: thanks — will post canary outcome in this thread. tagging @Jian for review when PR is up. :thumbsup:
